novelty.justification: “Scientific concepts that reflect genuine, dataset-independent mechanisms should be encoded in the shared subspace” proposes a per-concept measurement relationship: cross-model agreement indicates a real scientific mechanism and predicts OOD generalization, whereas model-specific encoding indicates shortcuts. Searches for “cross-model representational universality shared model-specific features,” “crosscoder model diffing shared features,” “representation similarity generalization CKA,” and “scientific foundation models convergent representations” identify close precedents in Huh et al.’s The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (2024), Towards Universality: Studying Mechanistic Similarity Across Language Model Architectures (2024), and Sparse Crosscoders for Cross-Layer Features and Model Diffing, which already associate independently learned agreement with shared abstractions and separate common from model-specific features. The proposed “Mechanism-Universality Score” is therefore a substantive natural extension and integration—distinct in using concept-level agreement to separate scientific mechanisms from artifacts and address annotation circularity, but not a new core representational paradigm.
